statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-109828: when libsndfile parses a LIST/adtl chunk in a WAV file, wavlike_subchunk_parse() in src/wavlike.c copies a fixed 256 bytes from the labl subchunk buffer into the cue-point name, so a short label pulls uninitialized stack memory into the name, which an application can read back through SFC_GET_CUE (https://github.com/libsndfile/libsndfile/issues/1169). The upstream fix copies only the label up to its terminator with psf_strlcpy (https://github.com/libsndfile/libsndfile/commit/1ccd2a18826722c3aa9ed54122ebff20e3b92b10, https://github.com/libsndfile/libsndfile/pull/1170). Debian lists trixie's 1.2.2-2+deb13u1 as unfixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-109828). This owner publishes three builds of Debian's 1.2.2-2+deb13u1 in the DHI Debian repository, each as libsndfile1, libsndfile1-dev and sndfile-programs with their dbgsym packages, for amd64 and arm64. Checked the libsndfile1 library and its debug symbols for every build on both architectures: in the newest build, at this range's fixed version, wavlike_subchunk_parse calls psf_strlcpy and its changelog records the backport of that upstream commit; in the two earlier builds the function makes no such call. The range places the earlier builds on the affected side and the newest build on the fixed side.
